name: Eliab
overview: Eliab was a male member of the tribe of Gad, recognized as the third among the Gadites who came to David at Ziklag. His arrival with others to support David marks his significance within the tribe's allegiance during this period. This identification highlights his role within the broader narrative of David's consolidation of support.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliab means 'G-d is my father,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names that expresses a personal relationship with God. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 12:9 and carries no indication of being divinely given but signifies his identity grounded in faith.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Eliab as a descendant of Gad, linking him to this tribal lineage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are documented for Eliab in the provided information.
scriptureSignificance: Eliab's significance lies in his role as one of the Gadite warriors who joined David at Ziklag, demonstrating the gathering of tribal support essential to David's rise. Although distinct from the more widely known Eliab of Jesse's family, his presence underscores the unity among Israel's tribes in recognizing David's leadership. His story contributes to the biblical theme of God raising leaders through the support of faithful followers across Israel.
